newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Construction starts at Saudi steel plants.
newsitem.headline: Construction starts at Saudi steel plants.

text.p: Construction work has started on two plants in Saudi Arabia that will raise the kingdom's steel and iron output to more than four million tonnes annually from the current 2.7 million tonnes per year, contractors said.

Both plants will be part of the Saudi Iron and Steel Company, known as Hadeed. Hadeed is owned by Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), which is 70 percent owned by the Saudi government.

Voest-Alpine Industrieanlagenbau (VAI), a unit of Austria's VA Technologie, and Germany's SMS Schloemann Siemag AG, a unit of MAN AG, are building a flat steel plant with a 850,000 tonnes annual capacity.

"Construction work has already started. We hope to be completed in the third quarter of 1988," VAI president and chief executive officer Horst Wiesinger told Reuters. He said the building contract was worth $880 million.
Davy International, a unit of Trafalgar House, part of Norwegian technology and engineering group Kvaerner A/S, is building a 1.1 million tonnes per year direct reduction plant to produce iron.
"The contract is worth $165 million and will come on stream at the end of the third quarter 1988," Mike Foster, executive vice president of Kvaerner told Reuters.
SABIC Vice-Chairman Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Salameh said the company's annual production of various products had exceeded 23 million tonnes and the company was investing more to boost production.
"Several expansion projects are underway to target an annual production of more than 28 million tonnes by the year 2000," he told a gathering in the industrial city of Jubail on Thursday.

Officials said a new 3.7 billion riyal MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether) for the Saudi Petrochemical Co (SADAF) had started production and would produce at full capacity of 700,000 tonnes a year starting next week.
SADAF is a joint venture between SABIC and Pecten Arabia Co, a unit of the U.S. Shell Oil Co, itself an affiliate of Royal Dutch Shell Group.
"The (MTBE) plant has been completed. It started production three days ago and would fully be operational next week," a SABIC official told Reuters.
The plant would raise the kingdom's capacity to 2.7 million tonnes from two million tonnes of MTBE, an additive that makes gasoline burn more cleanly.
SABIC accounts for five percent of total world output of petrochemicals.
It controls and operates 16 joint venture complexes with Western and Japanese companies, producing mainly petrochemicals plastics, fertilizers and steel.
